claim: Meiosis requires transient removal of the outer kinetochore, the complex that connects microtubules to chromosomes.
source: Meiosis requires transient removal of the outer kinetochore, the complex that connects microtubules to chromosomes.
evidence: This is a statement in the abstract that is supported by citations in the introduction and results sections.

claim: Kinetochore inactivation in budding yeast occurs by reducing the abundance of a limiting subunit, Ndc80.
source: We discovered that in budding yeast, kinetochore inactivation occurs by reducing the abundance of a limiting subunit, Ndc80.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 1.

claim: An alternate NDC80 mRNA isoform with an extended 5' leader cannot produce protein due to regulatory upstream ORFs.
source: Central to this mechanism is the developmentally controlled transcription of an alternate NDC80 mRNA isoform, which itself cannot produce protein due to regulatory upstream ORFs in its extended 5' leader.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 3.

claim: Transcription of the alternate NDC80 isoform represses the canonical NDC80 mRNA expression in cis.
source: Instead, transcription of this isoform represses the canonical NDC80 mRNA expression in cis, thereby inhibiting Ndc80 protein synthesis.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 4.

claim: Kinetochores do not bind to microtubules in meiotic prophase in multiple systems.
source: In multiple systems, it has been shown that kinetochores do not bind to microtubules in meiotic prophase (Asakawa et al., 2005; Kim et al., 2013; Meyer et al., 2015; Miller et al., 2012; Sun et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: Temporal inactivation of kinetochores is achieved through removal of the outer kinetochore.
source: Furthermore, this temporal inactivation is achieved through removal of the outer kinetochore, the site where microtubule attachments occur (Asakawa et al., 2005; Kim et al., 2013; Meyer et al., 2015; Miller et al., 2012; Sun et al., 2011) (Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations and a figure showing the schematic of kinetochore behavior.

claim: Cells that fail to disassemble the outer kinetochore undergo catastrophic missegregation of meiotic chromosomes.
source: In the presence of a spindle, cells that fail to disassemble the outer kinetochore undergo catastrophic missegregation of meiotic chromosomes, underlying the essential nature of kinetochore downregulation during meiotic prophase (Miller et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Ndc80 protein abundance decreases in meiotic prophase.
source: Consistent with this report, we found that even in an extended meiotic prophase arrest, Ndc80 was the only subunit of its complex whose abundance decreased at this meiotic stage (Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunoblot data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Nuf2, Spc24, and Spc25 are all expressed in meiotic prophase.
source: Nuf2, Spc24, and Spc25 were all expressed, though it has been reported that these proteins fail to localize to the kinetochores during meiotic prophase (Meyer et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunoblot data in Figure 1C and a citation.

claim: Ndc80 is the limiting kinetochore subunit in meiosis.
source: These observations raised the possibility that Ndc80 could be the limiting kinetochore subunit in meiosis.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that Ndc80 is the only subunit whose abundance decreases.

claim: Overexpression of NDC80 in meiotic prophase causes over 30% of cells to display abnormal segregation pattern in meiosis I.
source: When NDC80 was overexpressed in pCUP-CLB3 cells during meiotic prophase, over 30% of the cells displayed an abnormal segregation pattern in meiosis I.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Overexpression of NUF2, SPC24 or SPC25 does not enhance the segregation defect caused by CLB3 misexpression.
source: Importantly, this defect was not further enhanced by the overexpression of NUF2, SPC24 or SPC25 (Figure 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Ndc80 is the sole subunit of its complex that is tightly regulated during meiotic differentiation.
source: Together, these results demonstrate that Ndc80 is the sole subunit of its complex that is tightly regulated during meiotic differentiation and strongly support the notion that NDC80 downregulation and re-synthesis govern kinetochore functionality in meiosis.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data in Figure 1.

claim: Meiosis-specific RNA-seq reads extend to ~500 base pairs upstream of the NDC80 ORF.
source: Analysis of this dataset revealed the presence of meiosis-specific RNA-seq reads that extend to ~500 base pairs (bp) upstream of the NDC80 ORF (Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by analysis of published RNA-seq data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The extended RNA-seq reads appeared after meiotic entry and persisted until the end of meiosis.
source: These reads appeared after meiotic entry and persisted until the end of meiosis, but were absent during vegetative growth (Figure 2—figure supplement 1, vegetative) or starvation (Figure 2—figure supplement 1, MATa/MATa).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Two distinct NDC80 transcript isoforms exist in meiosis: a longer meiosis-specific isoform and a shorter isoform.
source: However, in cells undergoing synchronous meiosis, two distinct NDC80 transcript isoforms became evident: a longer, meiosis-specific isoform, and a shorter isoform that was also present under non-meiotic conditions (Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by northern blot data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The longer NDC80 isoform appeared after meiotic entry and persisted throughout meiotic prophase.
source: The longer isoform appeared after meiotic entry, persisted throughout meiotic prophase and gradually disappeared during the meiotic divisions.
evidence: This claim is supported by northern blot data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The shorter NDC80 isoform was weakly expressed during S phase and meiotic prophase but dramatically increased during the meiotic divisions.
source: The shorter isoform was present in vegetative cells prior to meiotic entry, but was weakly expressed during S phase and meiotic prophase. Its abundance dramatically increased during the meiotic divisions (Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplements 2B and 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by northern blot data shown in Figure 2B and supplementary figures.

claim: Ndc80 protein levels are higher when the shorter transcript is predominant and lower when the longer transcript is predominant.
source: Interestingly, the Ndc80 protein levels were noticeably higher during the meiotic stages when the shorter transcript was the predominant isoform, but lower when the longer transcript was predominant (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by northern and western blot data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The two NDC80 isoforms localize to both the nucleus and cytoplasm.
source: In addition, the two NDC80 isoforms localized to both the nucleus and cytoplasm (Figure 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by smFISH data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The expression of the long and short NDC80 isoforms are anti-correlated in meiosis.
source: Altogether, the combined analyses of northern and western blotting, as well as smFISH, reveal two interesting trends: (1) In meiosis, the expression of the long and short NDC80 isoforms are anti-correlated.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data in Figure 2.

claim: Ndc80 protein levels positively correlate with the presence of the short isoform and negatively correlate with the long isoform.
source: (2) Ndc80 protein levels positively correlate with the presence of the short isoform and negatively correlate with the long isoform (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data in Figure 2B.

claim: The longer NDC80 isoform contains nine uORFs, each with an AUG start codon.
source: In addition to the NDC80 ORF, the longer isoform contains nine uORFs, each with an AUG start codon.
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis of the longer isoform.

claim: The first six uORFs of the longer NDC80 isoform have ribosome profiling signatures consistent with them being translated in meiosis.
source: The first six of these uORFs, those closest to the 5' end of the mRNA, have ribosome profiling signatures consistent with them being translated in meiosis (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by ribosome profiling data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: When all nine AUGs of the uORFs are mutated, Ndc80 protein becomes highly abundant during meiotic prophase.
source: Indeed, when all nine AUGs were mutated, Ndc80 protein became highly abundant during meiotic prophase, even though the long isoform remained the predominant NDC80 transcript in these cells (Figure 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Translation of the uORFs represses translation of the NDC80 ORF from the long NDC80 isoform.
source: Therefore, translation of the uORFs represses translation of the NDC80 ORF from the long NDC80 isoform, rendering this isoform unable to synthesize Ndc80 protein.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data in Figure 3.

claim: The short NDC80 mRNA is capable of translating NDC80 ORF.
source: The shorter isoform is capable of translating NDC80 ORF.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the analyses and is consistent with the data showing Ndc80 protein is produced when the short isoform is present.

claim: The longer NDC80 mRNA does not support Ndc80 synthesis because uORF translation prevents ribosomes from accessing the actual ORF.
source: In contrast, although the longer isoform contains the entire ORF, it does not support Ndc80 synthesis. The coding information is not decoded from this isoform because uORF translation prevents ribosomes from accessing the actual ORF.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data in Figure 3.

claim: Deletion of the NDC80luti promoter results in detection of NDC80ORF during meiotic prophase.
source: As shown by northern blotting, NDC80ORF was detected during meiotic prophase in two different ∆NDC80luti mutant strains (Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by northern blot data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Deletion of NDC80luti causes Ndc80 protein levels to increase throughout meiotic prophase.
source: Accordingly, Ndc80 protein levels increased throughout meiotic prophase (Figure 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Early termination of NDC80luti results in persistence of NDC80ORF mRNA and Ndc80 protein in meiotic prophase.
source: We observed that, upon early termination of NDC80luti, NDC80ORF mRNA and Ndc80 protein persisted in meiotic prophase (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claim: Continuous transcription through the NDC80ORF promoter is necessary for NDC80ORF repression.
source: This observation suggests that continuous transcription through the NDC80ORF promoter is necessary for NDC80ORF repression.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the early termination experiment.

claim: The repression of NDC80ORF is not due to competition between the NDC80ORF promoter and the NDC80luti promoter for RNA polymerase and the general transcription machinery.
source: It also indicates that the repression of NDC80ORF is not due to competition between the NDC80ORF promoter and the NDC80luti promoter for RNA polymerase and the general transcription machinery.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the early termination experiment.

claim: NDC80luti-mediated repression occurs in cis.
source: This result demonstrates that NDC80luti-mediated repression occurs in cis, since NDC80luti cannot reduce Ndc80 protein expression from a copy of NDC80 on another chromosome (Figure 4D, right panel).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The promoter and 5' leader sequence of NDC80luti is sufficient to downregulate another protein (NUF2) in meiotic prophase.
source: This result demonstrates that the promoter and 5' leader sequence of NDC80luti is sufficient to downregulate another protein in meiotic prophase.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A and B.

claim: Expression of NDC80luti is sufficient to repress NDC80ORF outside of meiosis.
source: Based on these data, we conclude that NDC80luti expression is sufficient to repress NDC80ORF outside of meiosis.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C and D.

claim: Deletion of IME1 abolishes NDC80luti production and results in persistent levels of NDC80ORF transcript and Ndc80 protein.
source: Indeed, deletion of IME1 abolished NDC80luti production and resulted in persistent levels of NDC80ORF transcript and Ndc80 protein (Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: A consensus site for Ume6 is present 583 bp upstream of the Ndc80 translation start site.
source: Given the close relationship between Ime1 and Ume6, we inspected the 5' intergenic region of NDC80 and identified a consensus site for Ume6 583 bp upstream of the Ndc80 translation start site (Figure 6B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1), within the NDC80luti promoter.
evidence: This claim is based on sequence analysis shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Ume6 binding is enriched over the predicted URS1 site in mitosis and early meiosis.
source: ChIP analysis revealed that Ume6 binding was enriched over the predicted URS1 site in mitosis and early meiosis (Figure 6C and Figure 6—figure supplement 2), whereas Ume6 binding was undetectable within the NDC80ORF promoter (Figure 6C and Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Deletion of the URS1 site completely abolishes Ume6 binding to the NDC80luti promoter.
source: Deletion of the URS1 site (ndc80-urs1∆) completely abolished Ume6 binding to the NDC80luti promoter (Figure 6C), but did not affect another Ime1-Ume6 target gene IME2 (Figure 6—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Deletion of the URS1 site results in leaky expression of NDC80luti during vegetative growth.
source: Consistent with the role of Ume6 as a transcriptional repressor in mitosis, deletion of the URS1 site resulted in leaky expression of NDC80luti during vegetative growth (Figure 6D and E, p<0.0001) and reduced expression of NDC80ORF (Figure 6E, p=0.0057).
evidence: This claim is supported by smFISH data shown in Figure 6D and E.

claim: Ime1 and Ume6 directly regulate the transcription of NDC80luti.
source: We conclude that similar to early meiotic genes, Ime1 and Ume6 directly regulate the transcription of NDC80luti.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data in Figure 6.

claim: An Ndt80 consensus site (MSE) is present at 184 bp upstream of the Ndc80 translation start site.
source: Within the budding yeast lineage, an Ndt80 consensus site, called the mid-sporulation element (MSE), was identified at 184 bp upstream of the Ndc80 translation start site (Figure 6B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1), within the NDC80ORF promoter.
evidence: This claim is based on sequence analysis shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Ndt80 binding is enriched over the predicted MSE one hour after Ndt80 expression is induced.
source: One hour after Ndt80 expression was induced in the pGAL-NDT80 GAL4-ER system, Ndt80 binding was enriched over the predicted MSE by ChIP analysis; moreover, mutations in the MSE (ndc80-mse) led to a complete loss of Ndt80 enrichment (Figure 6F), but did not affect another Ndt80 target gene MAM1 (Figure 6—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 6F.

claim: Mutations in the MSE reduce both NDC80ORF transcript and Ndc80 protein levels during the meiotic divisions.
source: Furthermore, the defect in Ndt80 binding to the NDC80ORF promoter reduced both NDC80ORF transcript and Ndc80 protein levels during the meiotic divisions (Figure 6J).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6J.

claim: Ndt80 directly induces NDC80ORF expression after meiotic prophase.
source: These results demonstrate that Ndt80 directly induces NDC80ORF expression after meiotic prophase, and this timely induction of NDC80ORF elevates the levels of Ndc80 protein prior to the meiotic divisions.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data in Figure 6.

claim: Over 50% of ∆NDC80luti or ∆9AUG cells display abnormal chromosome segregation in meiosis I.
source: Using the same assay described in Figure 1D, we observed that over 50% of the ∆NDC80luti or ∆9AUG cells displayed abnormal chromosome segregation in meiosis I (Figure 7A), suggesting premature kinetochore activity in meiotic prophase.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Repression of NDC80ORF by NDC80luti transcription is crucial to inhibit untimely kinetochore function during meiotic prophase.
source: Therefore, repression of NDC80ORF by NDC80luti transcription is crucial to inhibit untimely kinetochore function during meiotic prophase.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data in Figure 7A.

claim: 98% of ndc80-mse cells fail to properly segregate chromosome V.
source: Only 1% of wild type cells missegregated chromosome V, whereas 98% of the ndc80-mse cells failed to properly segregate this chromosome (Figure 7B), suggesting that kinetochores are not functional in ndc80-mse cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: Ndt80-dependent induction of NDC80ORF is essential for re-establishing kinetochore function to mediate meiotic chromosome segregation.
source: All of these results demonstrate that Ndt80-dependent induction of NDC80ORF is essential for re-establishing kinetochore function to mediate meiotic chromosome segregation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data in Figure 7.

claim: Cells with deleted Ume6 repressor-binding site (urs1∆) have a severe growth defect at 37°C due to reduced Ndc80 levels.
source: Indeed, when the Ume6 repressor-binding site within the NDC80luti promoter was deleted (urs1∆), these cells grew similar to wild type cells at 30°C, but they had a severe growth defect at 37°C due to reduced Ndc80 levels (Figure 8A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8A and B.

claim: The repression of NDC80luti by Ume6 is critical for the fitness of mitotically dividing cells.
source: Thus, the repression of NDC80luti by Ume6 is critical for the fitness of mitotically dividing cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data in Figure 8A and B.

claim: Strong induction of NDC80luti in vegetative growth causes a severe growth defect.
source: When NDC80luti was strongly induced in vegetative growth using the inducible GAL1-10 promoter, these cells had a severe growth defect (Figure 8C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8C.

claim: The growth defect caused by NDC80luti induction is rescued by a second copy of NDC80 at an ectopic locus.
source: This defect was rescued by a second copy of NDC80 at an ectopic locus, consistent with the notion that NDC80luti-mediated repression of NDC80ORF occurs in cis (Figure 8C and Figure 4D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8C.

claim: Cells expressing NDC80luti display a range of kinetochore-microtubule attachment defects.
source: Cells expressing NDC80luti displayed a range of kinetochore-microtubule attachment defects (Figure 8E, bottom panel).
evidence: This claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 8E.

claim: The strict temporal regulation of NDC80luti and NDC80ORF transcription in both mitosis and meiosis is essential to ensure the proper timing of kinetochore function and high fidelity chromosome segregation.
source: Collectively, these analyses revealed that the strict temporal regulation of NDC80luti and NDC80ORF transcription in both mitosis and meiosis is essential to ensure the proper timing of kinetochore function and high fidelity chromosome segregation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data in Figure 8.

claim: The cell regulates the activity of the kinetochore complex by limiting the availability of a single subunit, Ndc80.
source: Thus, in the case of the meiotic kinetochore, the cell regulates the activity of a multi-protein complex by limiting the availability of a single subunit.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: NDC80luti is a bona fide mRNA that is poly-adenylated and engaged by the ribosome.
source: Indeed, NDC80luti is a bona fide mRNA. It is poly-adenylated, is engaged by the ribosome and, most importantly, when the uORF start codons are ablated, Ndc80 protein is translated from this extended mRNA isoform (Brar et al., 2012 and Figure 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by published data and experimental data in Figure 3.

claim: NDC80luti is likely a RNA Polymerase II transcript.
source: Moreover, NDC80luti is likely a RNA Polymerase II transcript because its promoter is occupied by the pre-initiation complex member Sua7 (TFIIB) and because Pol II-associated chromatin marks are detected downstream of the NDC80luti promoter when this transcript is made (Chia et al., accompanying manuscript).
evidence: This claim is supported by data from the accompanying manuscript.

claim: The polypeptides that the uORFs encode are unlikely to play a role in the repression of kinetochore function.
source: The polypeptides that the uORFs encode are unlikely to play a role in the repression of kinetochore function as the uORFs can be minimized to 2-codon units while maintaining NDC80luti-based repression (Figure 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Upstream AUG codons are present in the putative NDC80luti mRNAs predicted from other fungal species.
source: Interestingly, upstream AUG codons are also present in the putative NDC80luti mRNAs predicted from the other fungal species. Three regions were enriched for the presence of such AUGs (Figure 9—figure supplements 1 and 2), but the sequences and the length of these putative uORFs did not seem to be conserved (Supplementary file 1G).
evidence: This claim is supported by sequence analysis shown in Figure 9—figure supplements 1 and 2.

claim: The act of uORF translation, rather than the identity of the uORF peptides, serves as a conserved feature in evolution.
source: This observation is consistent with the idea that the act of uORF translation, rather than the identity of the uORF peptides, serves as a conserved feature in evolution.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the sequence analysis.

claim: The biological purpose of NDC80luti is to shut down Ndc80 protein synthesis by repressing NDC80ORF in cis.
source: We propose that the biological purpose of NDC80luti is to shut down Ndc80 protein synthesis by repressing NDC80ORF in cis, thereby inactivating kinetochore function during meiotic prophase.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: Transcription of NDC80luti introduces repressive chromatin marks at the NDC80ORF promoter that are necessary for the downregulation of NDC80ORF and Ndc80 protein.
source: Third, transcription of NDC80luti introduces repressive chromatin marks at the NDC80ORF promoter that are necessary for the downregulation of NDC80ORF and Ndc80 protein (Chia et al., accompanying manuscript).
evidence: This claim is supported by data from the accompanying manuscript.

claim: The primary function of the NDC80luti mRNA is to turn off the NDC80 gene.
source: Altogether, these findings strongly suggest that the primary function of the NDC80luti mRNA is to turn off the NDC80 gene.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: This mechanism of gene repression is both economical and highly flexible from an evolutionary point of view.
source: We would argue from an evolutionary point of view that this solution could be both economical and highly flexible.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the evolutionary advantages of the mechanism.

claim: The meiotic cell is co-opting two existing transcription factors, Ime1 and Ndt80, for roles in activating and repressing gene expression.
source: First, the meiotic cell is co-opting two existing transcription factors, Ime1 and Ndt80, for roles in activating and repressing gene expression, obviating the need to evolve novel trans-acting factors.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing Ime1 and Ndt80 regulate NDC80 isoforms.

claim: This study is the first clear demonstration that it is the choice of promoter and the identity of the resulting mRNA isoform that governs whether a gene is turned on or turned off by a given transcription factor.
source: While transcription factors have previously been implicated in the repression of downstream promoters (Bird et al., 2006; Martens et al., 2004; Shearwin et al., 2005; van Werven et al., 2012), our study is the first clear demonstration that it is the choice of promoter and the identity of the resulting mRNA isoform that governs whether a gene is turned on or turned off by a given transcription factor.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the study, supported by comparison to prior work.

claim: Analysis of mRNA-seq and ribosome profiling datasets of meiotic yeast revealed hundreds of transcripts with potential luti-like signatures.
source: Analysis of the mRNA-seq and ribosome profiling datasets of meiotic yeast revealed hundreds of transcripts with potential luti-like signatures (Brar et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is based on analysis of published datasets.

claim: Two other genes, ORC1 and BOI1, have been shown to express meiosis-specific transcript isoforms with uORF-containing leader extensions.
source: In support of this idea, two other genes, ORC1 and BOI1, have been shown to express meiosis-specific transcript isoforms with uORF-containing leader extensions (Xie et al., 2016 and Liu et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Alternative promoter usage is widespread in development and among different cell types.
source: Alternative promoter usage is widespread in development and among different cell types. For example, in the fruit fly, more than 40% of developmentally expressed genes have at least two promoters with distinct regulatory programs (Batut et al., 2013). Half of human genes have more than one promoter, resulting in the expression of mRNA isoforms with 5' heterogeneity (Kimura et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Transcription-based interference mechanisms and transcription-coupled histone modifications have been described in a variety of organisms.
source: Furthermore, transcription-based interference mechanisms, as well as transcription-coupled histone modifications, have been described in a variety of organisms (Corbin and Maniatis, 1989; Eissenberg and Shilatifard, 2010; Shearwin et al., 2005; Wagner and Carpenter, 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: uORF translation is much more widespread than traditionally believed and acts in a regulatory manner.
source: Finally, recent studies have shown that uORF translation is much more widespread than traditionally believed and acts in a regulatory manner (Calvo et al., 2009; Chew et al., 2016; Johnstone et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The regulatory circuit described in this study can be used as a roadmap in future studies to uncover transcription-coupled gene repression during cell fate transitions across multiple species.
source: Therefore, we envision that the regulatory circuit described here can be used as a roadmap in future studies to uncover transcription-coupled gene repression during cell fate transitions across multiple species.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the broader implications of the study.

claim: Multiple studies have reported poor correlation between mRNA and protein abundance.
source: Notably, multiple studies have reported poor correlation between mRNA and protein abundance (Maier et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: For mRNAs that anti-correlate with their protein levels, this apparent contradiction might be due to a luti-mRNA being misattributed as a canonical protein-coding transcript.
source: For those mRNAs that anti-correlate with their protein levels, this apparent contradiction might be due to a luti-mRNA being misattributed as a canonical protein-coding transcript.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the interpretation of prior studies.
